title: Asante weavers rework imported silk for kente
summary: Asante weavers unraveled imported silk cloth to obtain richly colored threads for kente, connecting local weaving skills with long-distance textile trade.

citations.locator: Kente cloth section: imported silk in eighteenth-century Asante weaving
citations.note: Supports the linked claims within the stated date and attribution limits.

claims.text: Asante weavers unraveled imported silk cloth to obtain richly colored threads for kente, connecting local weaving skills with long-distance textile trade.
Century-level evidence for the practice, not an exact invention date or the beginning of kente weaving.
Kente is assembled from narrow woven strips joined along their edges. Imported silk expanded the colors available to eighteenth-century Asante makers.

review.corroboration: The Met exhibition’s Kente cloth passage was inspected. An additional Met collection result was found but would not constitute a second source family.
